<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via attachedOnRead (symbol, a field of const object SysApprovalRequest))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0a26961394ff817918d6750a60bb6e0d641946ba` — the merge of head `e4fc3fec39bf94a1c1cda5942fae62881a14649f` into base `3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0a26961394ff817918d6750a60bb6e0d641946ba && git checkout 0a26961394ff817918d6750a60bb6e0d641946ba
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 e4fc3fec39bf94a1c1cda5942fae62881a14649f && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 && git merge --no-ff e4fc3fec39bf94a1c1cda5942fae62881a14649f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the delta record below. It was rendered on this head, at the contract-review tier, by the same isolated reviewer that recorded the earlier FAIL. The seat holds that FAIL record privately; mechanism detail stays with the security seat. The seat will file N1's follow-up card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e4fc3fec39bf94a1c1cda5942fae62881a14649f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-override-audit.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/exclude-submitter.integration.test.ts, content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx, .changeset/override-never-approves-own-request.md

### ① Derived judgments

- **Delta.** This is a delta review of the FAIL record at `496e6ff294`.
  - `66a6bbbc69` is a sync-only merge of `origin/main`: its tree equals the mechanical merge of its two parents, and `496e6ff294..66a6bbbc69` changes no file of this PR.
  - The reviewed delta is `66a6bbbc69..e4fc3fec39`: 5 files. It does not change the spec contract, the object file, or anything under `ui/`.
- **Unchanged since the earlier record:** the approve door, the viewer flag and the Approve predicate. Those judgments stand.
- **Reassign door.** A reassign admitted only through the override now has two rules:
  - Whoever makes it, a target that names the submitter, or a position only they hold, is refused.
  - When the submitter makes it, every target they could act under is refused, including a position shared with others.
  - A different administrator, and a slot holder under `excludeSubmitter`, keep the only-holder rule.
- **Over-refusal: none found.** These cases are each unchanged and pinned as controls:
  - a non-submitter administrator's reassign to a shared position;
  - the submitter-administrator's reassign to a position they do not hold;
  - a slot holder's hand-off.

  Reject and recall are untouched.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the earlier record:
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset.
- `patch` on both packages, and one ADR-0087 marker.

The changeset's BREAKING text now states the wider reassign refusal and what is not moved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Shared position, different administrator.** Left open by design, and now stated in the docs, the changeset and the PR body. It falls inside item 6: the submitter is one holder on a slate someone else chose.
- **`admin_rescue` after recall and resubmit.** Inside item 6, as before. The docs now say who is on that slate.
- **Dev deviation: the letter-case pin runs on a store double.** Adequate.
  - The comparison is a pure function that does not depend on the store. The double only stands in for a store that resolves the target, which the SQLite harness cannot do.
  - The ablation turns that case red, so the pin holds the behaviour.
  - No real case-folding store is in the suite; see N3.
- **Dogfood battery not re-run at this head.** Accepted. The delta reaches no door status or code that the door-level pins assert, and CI ran the suites at this head.
- **SQL push-down.** No new read. Both rules reuse the position expansion the check already makes.

### ④ Design judgment

**Findings of the earlier record**

- **M1: closed.** `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts:7543-7578`. Pinned on a real engine and position directory at `exclude-submitter.integration.test.ts:370`. The pins cover id, email, a sole-held position and a shared position; the shared position with `excludeSubmitter` on; and two controls.
- **M2: closed.** `approval-service.ts:1282` (`slotsName`), read on every comparison of the check (`:7550`, `:7551`, `:7569`, `:7570`). Pinned at `approval-override-audit.test.ts:321`.
- **S1: closed.** `exclude-submitter.integration.test.ts:370`, on `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`: the position arm for the submitter and for a different administrator.
- **S2: closed.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:1013-1019`.
- **S3: closed.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:1038-1046`. The three ways a bypassed approver keeps a read match the read gate.
- **N1: open, declared.** The PR body lists the four stale texts under "Follow-up owed", for the seat to file as one card.
- **N2: closed.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:597-599`.

**Contract.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` is unchanged in the delta, so the earlier judgment stands. The replacement PR body, the changeset and the docs now claim only what the code enforces, and each names the case left to `excludeSubmitter`.

**New findings**

- **N3 (nit).** The letter-case rule has no coverage on a real case-folding store. Not owed by this PR; worth a line on the follow-up card if a MySQL lane exists.
- **N4 (nit).** The unit test at `approval-override-audit.test.ts:321` replaces `engine.find` on the shared double and does not restore it in the case body. If the double is not rebuilt per case, later cases inherit the folded lookup. The suite is green, so this is hygiene only.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-fpj3`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
